items.title: Karma Ripening in This Life, the Next, or Some Life Beyond

items.zh: 順現法受業者，謂能感現法果業。順生受業者，謂能感無間生果業。順後受業者，謂能感彼後生果業。
items.en: Karma ripening in this very life is karma capable of bringing its result within this same lifetime. Karma ripening in the next life is karma capable of bringing its result in the immediately following life, without any gap between. Karma ripening in some later life is karma capable of bringing its result only from the life after next onward.

items.title: Three Times, Three Realms, and Three Levels of Training

items.zh: 過去業者，謂住習氣位，或已與果、或未與果業。未來業者，謂未生未滅業。現在業者，謂已造、已思、未謝滅業。
items.en: Past karma abides in the state of a habitual seed, whether it has already yielded its result or not yet. Future karma has neither yet arisen nor yet ceased. Present karma has already been performed, already been intended, and has not yet passed away.

items.zh: 欲繫業者，謂能感欲界異熟，墮欲界業。色繫業者，謂能感色界異熟，墮色界業。無色繫業者，謂能感無色界異熟，墮無色界業。
items.en: Karma bound to the desire realm brings a ripened result there. Karma bound to the form realm brings a ripened result there. Karma bound to the formless realm brings a ripened result there.

items.zh: 學業者，謂若異生、若非異生，學相續中所有善業。無學業者，謂無學相續中所有善業。非學非無學業者，謂除前二，餘相續中所有善、不善、無記業。
items.en: Karma of one still in training is every wholesome deed arising in the mind-stream of someone — whether an ordinary being or not — who has entered training. Karma of one beyond training is every wholesome deed arising in the mind-stream of an arhat. Karma of neither is every wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral deed arising in every remaining mind-stream, apart from these two.

items.title: Karma Abandoned by Seeing, by Cultivation, or Never Needing Abandonment

items.zh: 見所斷業者，謂受惡趣不善等業。修所斷業者，謂受善趣善、不善、無記業。無斷業者，謂世出世諸無漏業。
items.en: Karma abandoned by seeing is unwholesome karma, and the like, that leads to an unfortunate destiny. Karma abandoned by cultivation is wholesome, unwholesome, and neutral karma that leads to a fortunate destiny. Karma needing no abandonment at all is every uncontaminated deed, whether worldly or transcending the world.

items.title: Dark and Bright Karma, and the Fourth Kind That Ends Them All

items.zh: 黑黑異熟業者，謂非福業。白白異熟業者，謂不動業。黑白黑白異熟業者，謂福業。有不善業為惡對故，由約未斷非福業時所有福業而建立故。
items.en: Dark karma with a dark ripening is demeritorious karma. Bright karma with a bright ripening is unmoving karma. Mixed karma with a mixed ripening is meritorious karma — established precisely because unwholesome karma still stands as its unresolved counterpart, this naming applying at the stage when demeritorious karma has not yet been eliminated even while meritorious karma is being performed.

items.zh: 非黑非白無異熟業能盡諸業者，謂出世間諸無漏業，是前三業斷對治故。
items.en: Karma that is neither dark nor bright, carrying no ripening at all, capable of exhausting every other kind of karma, is transcendent uncontaminated karma — precisely because it serves as the antidote that severs all three of the preceding kinds.

items.title: Crooked, Tainted, and Turbid Karma, Against Pure and Tranquil — the Taxonomy Closes

items.zh: 曲業者，謂諸外道善不善業。穢業者，謂即曲業亦名穢業。又有穢業，謂此法異生於聖教中顛倒見者、住自見取者、邪決定者、猶預覺者所有善不善業。濁業者，謂即曲業、穢業亦名濁業。又有濁業，謂此法異生於聖教中不決定者、猶預覺者所有善不善業。
items.en: Crooked karma is the wholesome and unwholesome karma of every non-Buddhist teacher. Tainted karma is this same crooked karma, so named again; and there is a further tainted karma — the wholesome and unwholesome karma of one who, though within this very teaching, holds a distorted view of the sacred doctrine, clings fixedly to their own opinion, has settled into a wrong conclusion, or remains caught in doubt. Turbid karma is this same crooked and tainted karma, so named yet again; and there is a further turbid karma — the wholesome and unwholesome karma of one who, though within this very teaching, remains undecided about the sacred doctrine or caught in doubt.

items.zh: 又有差別，唯於外道法中有此三業。由邪解行義故，名曲；由此為依，能障所起諸功德義故，名穢；能障通達真如義故，名濁；應知。清淨業者，謂此法異生於聖教中正決定者、不猶預覺者所有善業。寂靜業者，謂住此法非異生者，一切聖者所有學無學業。
items.en: On a further reading, these three belong to non-Buddhist teachings alone. They are named crooked because they arise from wrongful understanding and wrongful conduct; named tainted because, on this same basis, they obstruct whatever wholesome quality would otherwise arise; and named turbid because they obstruct the realisation of suchness itself — so it should be understood. Pure karma is the wholesome karma of one who, within this very teaching, holds a settled and correct conviction about the sacred doctrine, free of doubt. Tranquil karma is the karma, whether still in training or beyond it, of every noble one who dwells in this teaching and is no longer an ordinary being at all.

items.title: Karma's Faults — Seven Kinds of Harm, and Karmic Defilement Closes

items.zh: 業過患云何？當知略說有七過患。謂殺生者殺生為因，能為自害、能為他害、能為俱害、生現法罪、生後法罪、生現法後法罪，受彼所生身心憂苦。
items.en: What are karma's faults? Briefly, there are seven. Taking killing as the cause: it can harm oneself, it can harm another, it can harm both; it generates guilt in this very life, guilt in a later life, or guilt in both this life and a later one; and it brings the resulting suffering of body and mind.

items.zh: 云何能為自害？謂為害生發起方便，由此因緣，便自被害，若被繫縛，若遭退失，若被訶毀；然彼不能損害於他。云何能為他害？謂即由此所起方便，能損害他。由此因緣，不自被害乃至訶毀。云何能為俱害？謂即由此所起方便，能損害他。由此因緣，復被他害，若被繫縛乃至訶毀。
items.en: What is harming oneself? One sets out to take a life, and by this very cause is oneself harmed in turn — seized and bound, stripped of one's own merit, or reviled — without ever having actually harmed the other. What is harming another? By this same undertaking, one does harm the other, and by this cause is not oneself harmed, bound, or reviled at all. What is harming both? By this same undertaking, one does harm the other, and by this same cause is in turn harmed oneself as well — seized, bound, or reviled in turn.

items.zh: 云何生現法罪？謂如能為自害。云何生後法罪？謂如能為他害。云何生現法後法罪？謂如能為俱害。云何受彼所生身心憂苦？謂為害生發起方便，而不能成六種過失。又不能辦隨欲殺事，彼由所欲不會因緣，便受所生身心憂苦。
items.en: What is generating guilt in this very life? It is as in harming oneself. What is generating guilt in a later life? It is as in harming another. What is generating guilt in both? It is as in harming both. And what is the resulting suffering of body and mind? One sets out to take a life, yet accomplishes none of the six faults just named, nor even succeeds in the killing itself — and simply from this failure to obtain what one sought, suffering of body and mind arises all the same.

items.zh: 又有十種過患，依犯尸羅。如經廣說應知。又有四種不善業道，及飲諸酒以為第五，依犯事善男學處，佛薄伽梵說多過患應知。廣說如闡地迦經。
items.en: There are, further, ten faults tied to breaking moral discipline, as the sūtras explain at length. And there are, further, the four unwholesome courses of action — killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and false speech — together with the drinking of intoxicants as a fifth: on the breach of any of these five lay precepts, the Blessed Buddha spoke of many faults, as explained at length in the Chanti-jia Sūtra.

items.title: Rebirth Defilement Opens: Four Aspects, and Fifty-Eight Places to Be Born

items.zh: 云何生雜染？謂由四種相應知。一、由差別故；二、由艱辛故；三、由不定故；四、由流轉故。生差別者，當知復有五種。一、界差別，二、趣差別，三、處所差別，四、勝生差別，五、自身世間差別。
items.en: What is rebirth defilement? It should be understood through four aspects: difference, hardship, uncertainty, and transmigration. Difference itself has five further kinds: difference of realm, difference of destiny, difference of place, difference of superior birth, and difference of one's own world.

items.zh: 界差別者，謂欲界及色無色界生差別。趣差別者，謂於五趣四生差別。處所差別者，謂欲界中有三十六處生差別，色界中有十八處生差別，無色界中有四處生差別，如是總有五十八生。
items.en: Difference of realm is the difference between birth in the desire realm and birth in the form or formless realm. Difference of destiny is the difference among the five destinies and the four modes of birth. Difference of place is thirty-six places of birth in the desire realm, eighteen in the form realm, and four in the formless realm — fifty-eight places of birth in all.

blocks.text: Today finishes the taxonomy of karma and its faults, completing karmic defilement, and opens the third kind, **rebirth defilement**. The most important single passage is the classical fourfold division of dark and bright karma, which includes a fourth kind of karma that ends all karma.

Karma ripens in this life, the next, or some later life. Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Pīxún jì*: a deed ripens in this life when it has heightened intent, heightened effort, and a superior field (Day 60).

subs.head: Three times, three realms, three trainings

blocks.text: Past karma "abides in the state of a habitual seed, whether it has already yielded its result or not". This is Day 40's answer to the Sarvāstivāda in a sentence. Karma is also classified as of trainees, of those beyond training, and of neither. Venerable Miào Jìng: "ordinary beings" in this classification means only Dharma students who have not yet seen the path.

subs.head: Abandoned by seeing or by cultivation

blocks.text: Karma abandoned by the path of seeing is unwholesome karma leading to unfortunate destinies, "and the like". Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the *Yujia lunji*, lists what the "and the like" covers: karma for a female rebirth, for an eighth human life (a stream-enterer has at most seven), for the heaven of no perception, for Uttarakuru.

items: **Dark karma with dark ripening**: demeritorious karma.
**Bright karma with bright ripening**: unmoving karma (the meditative realms).
**Mixed karma with mixed ripening**: meritorious karma of the desire realm, which is never wholly free of affliction.
**Neither dark nor bright, with no ripening**: the uncontaminated karma of the path, "which ends all karma".

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi adds a second reading of "mixed": an act whose motive is dark but whose appearance is bright, like a free offer made deceitfully in order to sell. The fourth kind is the point of the list. The aim is not more bright karma but karma that produces no further existence at all.

subs.head: Crooked, tainted, turbid; pure and tranquil

blocks.text: "**Crooked** karma is the wholesome and unwholesome karma of every non-Buddhist teacher." Master Cháng Bǎi: "The Dharma says a straight mind is the path." **Tainted** karma includes that of one who has "settled into a wrong conclusion", which Venerable Miào Jìng explains as concluding that all things are simply empty, the error of Day 50. **Tranquil** karma is the karma of noble ones.

Karma can harm oneself, another, or both; bring guilt now, later, or both; and produce bodily and mental suffering. Venerable Miào Jìng notes that drinking intoxicants is listed with the four unwholesome courses but belongs to the "preventive" precepts: not wrong in itself, but the door to the others.

The third kind of defilement is understood through four aspects: **difference** (the places and kinds of birth), **hardship**, **uncertainty**, and **transmigration**. Master Cháng Bǎi: these four show life to be suffering from four sides. There are fifty-eight places of birth: thirty-six in the desire realm, eighteen in the form realm, and four in the formless realm, the totals we counted on Day 23.

quiz.q: Citing the Pixunji, what makes karma able to ripen in this life, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: heightened intent, heightened effort, and a superior field — effort meaning uninterrupted, earnest, continuous, encouraging others, and rejoicing
quiz.why: *Pixunji*: "If a deed has heightened intent, heightened effort, and a superior field, it ripens in this very life." Master Cháng Bǎi: "If heightened effort has five conditions — uninterrupted, earnest, continuous, encouraging others, and rejoicing — it brings a present-life result." Venerable Miào Jìng: offering to an arhat who has attained cessation brings immediate results.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is past karma?
options: karma abiding as a habitual seed, whether it has yielded its result or not
quiz.why: "Past karma abides in the state of a habitual seed, whether it has already yielded its result or not yet." Future karma has neither arisen nor ceased; present karma has been done and intended but not yet passed away. Master Cháng Bǎi: "not arisen" excludes the present, "not ceased" the past.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what are dark-dark, bright-bright, and mixed karma?
options: dark-dark is demerit, bright-bright is unmoving karma, mixed is merit
quiz.why: "Dark karma with a dark ripening is demeritorious karma. Bright karma with a bright ripening is unmoving karma. Mixed karma with a mixed ripening is meritorious karma." Merit is "mixed" because unresolved demerit still stands against it. Venerable Miào Jìng: dark-dark means both cause and result are dark.

quiz.q: Master Cháng Bǎi gives another reading of mixed karma. What is it?
options: the motive is dark but the act bright — like offering free benefits out of deceit, really to make a sale
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Some people's motive is dark but their action bright — e.g. practising good with a deceitful mind, offering free benefits first in order to do business." He also gives the reverse: a teacher scolding a disciple — bright motive, dark means.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what is crooked karma?
options: the wholesome and unwholesome karma of non-Buddhist teachers
quiz.why: "Crooked karma is the wholesome and unwholesome karma of every non-Buddhist teacher." Master Cháng Bǎi: "The Dharma says a straight mind is the path; non-Buddhists' minds aren't straight, so their karma is crooked."

quiz.q: According to the treatise, which list gives karma's seven faults?
options: harm to self, to another, to both; guilt now, later, both; and resulting suffering of body and mind
quiz.why: "It can harm oneself, it can harm another, it can harm both; it generates guilt in this very life, guilt in a later life, or guilt in both this life and a later one; and it brings the resulting suffering of body and mind." Venerable Miào Jìng: self-harm begins with planning and setting out to kill, only to be harmed oneself.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, through which four aspects is rebirth defilement understood?
quiz.why: "It should be understood through four aspects: difference, hardship, uncertainty, and transmigration." Master Cháng Bǎi: these four reveal life to be full of affliction and ignorance. Difference has five kinds: realm, destiny, place, superior birth, one's own world.
